HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE NARENDRA SINGH DHADDHA
Judgment Date of Judgment 10/05/2024

The present appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 has been preferred by the appellant-claimant (for short 'the claimant') dissatisfied with the judgment and award dated 03.05.2017 passed by Special Court Printing & Stationary Embezzlement Cases &
Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Jaipur (for short 'the Tribunal') in claim case No.279/2017,
whereby the Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.2,46,300/- along with interest @ 7.5% per annum from the date of filing the claim petition in favour of the claimant.

sentences.text: [CMA-4274/2017] The Tribunal on the basis of the pleading of the parties, framed the issues and evaluated the evidence on record.
After hearing counsel for the parties, decided the claim petition of the claimant and awarded the amount as indicated above.
Learned counsel for the claimant submits that the Tribunal while passing the impugned judgment and award has not appreciated the evidence led by the claimant in the right perspective.
Learned counsel for the claimant further submits that the Tribunal has wrongly assessed the income of the claimant only Rs.4,500/- per month.
The claimant was earning Rs.6,000/- to Rs.7,000/- per month by agricultural and milk vending work.

So, income of the claimant may be considered Rs.6,000/-

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the claimant also submits that the Tribunal has wrongly considered permanent disability sustained by the claimant as 17.5% but as per evidence, left leg of claimant was shortened, so the claimant is entitled to get Rs.4 lacs towards shortening of left leg.
The Tribunal has not awarded towards future prospects, whereas as per age of the claimant i.e. 46 years, it should be 25% of the claimant's income.
So, the judgment and award of the Tribunal may be modified accordingly.

Learned counsel for the claimant has placed reliance upon the following judgments:- (1) Fareed Vs.
Mahaveer & Ors. reported in MACD 2010(1) (Raj.) 56 & (2) Swatantra Kumar Vs. Qamar Ali & Ors.
reported in 1998 ACJ 920.

sentences.text:
Learned counsel for the respondent No.3-SBI General Insurance Company Limited (for short 'the Insurance Company') has opposed the arguments advanced by learned counsel for the claimant and submitted that as per permanent disability (3 of 4) [CMA-4274/2017] certificate(Exhibit-15),
claimant sustained 17.5% permanent disability but the Tribunal has wrongly considered 18%
permanent disability of the claimant.

Learned counsel for the insurance company further submits that the claimant failed to adduce any cogent evidence that he was earning Rs.7,000/- to Rs.8,000/-
per month.
The Tribunal has rightly considered the claimant's income i.e. Rs.4,500/- per month.

So,
the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal does not require any interference.
So, the appeal filed by the claimant be dismissed.
I have considered the arguments advanced by learned counsel for the claimant as well as learned counsel for the Insurance Company.
It is an admitted position that the claimant failed to adduce any cogent evidence that he was earning Rs.7,000/- to Rs.8,000/- per month.
So, in my considered opinion, the Tribunal has rightly assessed the income of the claimant as Rs.4,500/- per month.

The Tribunal has determined 17.5%
loss of income viz-a-viz 17.5% permanent disability.
So, in my considered opinion, there is no need to grant any extra amount towards shortened of leg of the claimant.
The Tribunal has not awarded any amount towards future prospects, whereas as per age of the claimant i.e. 46 years, it should be 25% of his income.

So, the judgment of the Tribunal is modified to the extent as under:-
Annual income 4500 X 12 = Rs.54,000/-
As per age of the claimant i.e. 54000X13=Rs. 7,02,000/- 46 years, multiplier to be applied Loss of Income viz-a-viz was 7,02,000X 18% = Rs.1,26,360/-
18% permanent disability suffered by the claimant  (4 of 4) 
 Add 25% towards future 1,26,360 +
 prospects 25%) = Rs.

sentences.text:
Less amount awarded by the  Tribunal Rs. 2,46,300/-
 Enhanced amount of  compensation Rs. 31
In view of the above, the claimant is entitled to get a further sum of Rs. 31,650/- as compensation.

The Insurance Company is directed to deposit enhanced amount of Rs. 31,650/- (2,77,950- 2,46,300) with the Tribunal within a period of two months from the date of receipt of certified copy of this order.
On deposition of the said amount, the claimant shall be entitled to withdrawn the same.
The enhanced amount shall carry @ 7.5% interest per annum from the date of filing the claim petition till the actual payment is made.
Rest part of the impugned judgment shall remain unchanged.
Impugned judgment and award is modified accordingly.
Consequently, the appeal is partly allowed.
Pending application(s), if any, also stand(s) disposed of.
